newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW-German May BME/Reuters PMI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-German May BME/Reuters PMI.

text.p: The BME/Reuters German Purchasing Managers' Index rose to a seasonally-adjusted 57.49 in May from 56.58 in April, research group NTC Publications Ltd said in a statement released on Monday.
On an unadjusted basis it fell to 57.42 from 57.93.

The index, launched last month and available exclusively on Reuters systems, shows that on a seasonally-adjusted basis manufacturing activity expanded for the ninth consecutive month in May, NTC said.
Following are analysts' comments on the index.

Timo Klein, at MMS said the numbers were "as expected. The uptrend is still intact and the figures do not show the economy is really picking up tremendously in speed, the employment situation is still dire".
"I would be hesitant to call the development in employment really bouncing. Wage pressures are a long way off to put it mildly."

Guenther Redeker, Chase Investment: "This is obviously supporting the recent trend. I expect that gain to continue in Q2 and will have as well improvements in Q3. We are still looking at GDP growth rate at 2.25 pct, below the average of 2.5 pct....because of weakness in the labour market.
"On Friday's jobless I am looking for an unadjusted 160,000 decrease. On GDP, I am looking for 0.5 pct GDP increase, with new order figures showing a one pct increase.
"We have recently seen a nice move in raw materials to the upside, which is leading to higher import prices, but we still cannot really talk about domestic price pressure."

On short-term outlook for deutschemark: "There is still some hope because it is questionable whether government will get the majority it needs to change the Bundesbank law. I've heard there will be a vote either on June 27 or July 4 and already we have three members of parliament saying they will vote (in favour) of the Bundesbank, so the government is in real danger. But there must also be some negotiation between government and Bundesbank so that neither party loses face."

Rainer Schroeder, LGT - "The positive news is obviously that the decline in employment is coming to a stop. What we do need is the increase in exports and that is happening at the moment. We've got some quite restrictive fiscal policy, as we need, and that is why domestic demand will not pick up.
As long as economic expansion is as low as it is, we don't expect (price pressure) difficulties. There are no stability problems involved in these figures."
